prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
`heading_offset` (0–5, default 0, otherwise `ValueError`) is added to `markdown.Markdown` / `markdown.markdown`, with `--heading-offset N` on the command line. The full suite passes (1152 tests, 112 skipped); flake8 is not installed here, so lint was not run.

It is implemented as a new `heading_offset` tree processor that runs before all the others, so hash, underline and `md_in_html` headings are shifted before `toc` reads them. `toc` tokens and `toc_depth` therefore use the shifted levels, and `toc`'s `baselevel` stacks on top of the offset.

Behaviours you might not expect:
- Raw HTML headings that Markdown passes through untouched (a plain `<h1>` block) are not shifted. A raw heading nested inside an `md_in_html` `markdown="1"` block is shifted, because that extension parses it into the document tree.
- Only real integers are accepted: `True`, `1.0` and `'1'` all raise `ValueError`.
- On the command line an out-of-range or non-integer value exits with a usage error (code 2) rather than a traceback.

Docs are updated in `docs/library.md`, `docs/cli.md` and `docs/extensions/toc.md`, with an Unreleased changelog entry. I also added the missing `-n, --no_lazy_ol` line to the help listing in `docs/cli.md`.
